title: 病 · illness, disease, to fall ill, fault
desc: A person sweating on a sickbed with the phonetic 丙 inside: the radical 疒 frames every Chinese word for being unwell.

title: 春 · spring, springtime, vitality, the stir of desire
desc: Sun pressing up through young shoots: the season of growth, and the oldest Chinese metaphor for life-force and erotic longing.

title: 富 · rich, wealthy, abundant, to enrich
desc: A full wine jar tucked under a roof: the picture of a household storehouse packed to its rafters with plenty.

title: 父 · father, male elder, household head
desc: A hand gripping a stone axe: the tool of the one who heads the household, drawn as the figure of the father himself.

title: 哥 · elder brother, a familiar term for an older young man
desc: Two 可 stacked into one glyph; the doubled phonetic came to carry the warmest word in the family, elder brother.

title: 馆 · a public building, hall, shop, establishment
desc: A food-radical building: the eating-house that grew into the library, the museum, and the embassy.

title: 害 · to harm, injury, calamity, to fear
desc: Under the roof a mouth and a blade build the sense of injury done; the same glyph also means to fear, as in 害怕.

title: 喝 · to drink; (hè) to shout, to cry out
desc: A mouth radical paired with the phonetic 曷, splitting cleanly into the everyday hē you drink with and the older hè you shout with.

title: 河 · river, the Yellow River
desc: 河 began as the personal name of one river, the Yellow River, before it widened to mean any river at all.

title: 湖 · lake, the provinces around Dongting
desc: A water radical against the phonetic 胡, naming every still inland water from West Lake to the jianghu of wandering swordsmen.

title: 黄 · yellow, gold, the imperial color; to fall through
desc: The color of loess soil and the emperor, of the mother river and the egg yolk, and the one color slang that means a plan has collapsed.

title: 活 · to live, to be alive, lively, work
desc: Water gives the verb its life: a stream over a tongue, the flow that means being alive, and from there everything that moves, breathes, and gets done.

title: 鸡 · chicken, fowl, rooster
desc: The simplified 鸡 swaps a chicken-coop hand 又 in where the traditional 雞 kept the sound-bearer 奚 beside the bird.

title: 急 · urgent, anxious, hasty, rapid
desc: A heart pressed from above: 急 stacks a phonetic element over 心, so the glyph itself feels the squeeze of urgency.

title: 价 · price, value, worth
desc: A person standing beside 介 jiè: the worth a thing takes on only once two people sit down to trade for it.

title: 简 · simple, brief, terse; a bamboo writing slip
desc: Before paper, a letter was a strip of bamboo; from that narrow slip 简 grew into the words for simple, brief, and a short note.

title: 接 · to connect, to join, to receive, to meet
desc: The hand that joins: 接 puts a wrist behind every link, every catch, and every arrival you go out to greet.

title: 街 · street, avenue, thoroughfare
desc: The walk radical 行 splits open into a crossroads, and the jade-tablet phonetic 圭 sits inside, marking the place where roads cross and people pass.

title: 借 · to borrow, to lend, to make use of
desc: One glyph carries both halves of a loan: 借 means borrow and lend at once, the direction settled only by context.

title: 紧 · tight, taut, tense, urgent
desc: Thread drawn taut over the silk radical; the same word carries a tight knot, a tense nerve, an urgent deadline, and a tight wallet.
